result:
I changed the delivering-an-initiative skill (`skills/delivering-an-initiative/SKILL.md`) for r17 and r18 and committed it as `db77ded`. I ran no tests and no red or green cycle, because delivery has no scenarios: it is a guarantees capability, so the plan's red was the skill text read against r17 and r18.

- **r18:** a new drafting step runs before the first `work add`. The skill reads `features/` for scenarios tagged with a requirement from the proposals' `adds:` and `changes:`. If any names a requirement no planned work-item accepts, it stops and names each one by feature file and title. It runs no `work add`, so no work-item is committed.
- **r17:** a new step after each `work add` appends a `## Retires` section to the work-item's file. Each line holds the exact title of a `@deprecated` scenario whose own `@r<n>` tag names an accepted requirement, with its ` (deprecated)` suffix, in quotes, plus its feature file. If no scenario matches, it adds no section.
- **Commit step:** the "Commit them, alone" step now says `work add` has already committed each work-item. The pathspec commit then covers only the Retires sections, and only when there is a change.

The suite record at the start was 686 passed and 0 failed. `tools size --limit 300` printed nothing, and no tests were changed under an allowance. The plan contained no code.

The plan left four cases open, and I left them unchosen in the report's open questions:
- How to tell which scenarios the formulation "added or reworded". I used scenarios tagged with a requirement from the proposals' adds and changes.
- A deprecated scenario whose tags name requirements accepted by two work-items. The wording lists it under both.
- A `@deprecated` scenario with no `@r<n>` tag. It is listed nowhere.
- A re-run on existing work-items. Only work-items drafted in the current run get a Retires section.

The result file says `DONE` and the report is `report.md` in the run directory.
